Maintenance Report — MNT-0198-002

Asset: WELL-0198 (NE-08 Well 198, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 18 Jan 2023 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 458 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0198-0011 on 2022-12-29 Report written: 19 Jan 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0198-0011 showed the wellhead at 17.0 °C with the air at 6.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,881
Bolts, shims and seals470
Bearing grease and consumables784
Labour (company crew and contractor)2,250
Total5,385

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 6 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0198-003

Asset: WELL-0198 (NE-08 Well 198, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 20 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 20 Jan 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0198-0014 on 2023-01-19 Report written: 20 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0198-0014 at 13:00 on 2023-01-19 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.9% of the pad area, estimated 4.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 276 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 221 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0198-003 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.84% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

Absorbents and berms765
Soil hauling and disposal1,339
Labour (company crew and contractor)2,577
Total6,403

Maintenance Report — MNT-0198-008

Asset: WELL-0198 (NE-08 Well 198, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 03 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 Sep 2023 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 72 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0198-0046 on 2023-08-31 Report written: 08 Sep 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0198-0046 showed the wellhead at 34.0 °C with the air at 28.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Send the old pump for teardown.
